fact: The IATI record of a Korean-funded capacity-building grant refers to the Sierra Leone Government's National Innovation and Digital Strategy (2019-2029), a stated period that includes 2026; the record is dated 2026-01-01 and does not link the text. Text public: not stated

The article says the National Digital Development Policy (NDDP) was 'approved' in 2021 and aims to position Sierra Leone as an inclusive digital economy and society; it names no approving act or body.

The MTNDP 2024-2030 lists among the government's CTI-sector milestones of the 2019-2023 plan period the 'launch' of the national digital development policy, naming no approving act or body and no date within that period; as_of is the plan's January 2024 date.

The January 2023 National Data Strategy treats the 'National Digital Development Strategy of 2022' as an existing instrument and a 'key tool' for advancing the Medium-Term National Development Plan 2019-2023, with priorities across governance, infrastructure, skills, digital government, e-commerce and financial services, innovation, and cybersecurity and data; it uses no adoption verb and names no act or body.

The January 2023 National Data Strategy treats the 'National Digital Development Policy of 2021' as an existing instrument and a 'key tool' for advancing the Medium-Term National Development Plan 2019-2023, covering a broader digital ecosystem than the data strategy does; it uses no adoption verb and names no act or body.

The January 2023 GIZ assessment lists the 'National Innovation & Digital Strategy 2019-2029' among existing health and ICT frameworks, whose period includes January 2023; it cites it as a footnote and does not link the text. Text public: not stated

The Strategy, issued by the Ministry of Information and Communications and dated December 2022, says the NDDP/NDDS project was 'accelerated and finalized in 2021' and that the Strategy sets 'a holistic national digital agenda' over seven focus areas; it names no approving act or body.

The Strategy's next steps ask that the new USD 50,000,000 World Bank grant for the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project be used for initiatives that reflect the NDDS, and name no domestic budget line for the Strategy.

The Strategy says the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI), created in the State House in 2018, 'launched' the National Innovation and Digital Strategy (NIDS) (2019-2029), consistent with the NDDS; it names no approving act and does not describe the strategy's scope; as_of is the Strategy's December 2022 date.
The Strategy states the period of the National Innovation and Digital Strategy (NIDS) as 2019-2029, which includes December 2022; it does not link the text. Text public: not stated

The document, the National Digital Development Policy 2021 (a whole-of-government, whole-of-society policy across ten focus areas covering the digital economy and digital government), calls itself 'launched' in its unsigned foreword; it names no adopting act or body, and its design section records draft-policy consultation workshops held 28 September to 1 October 2021.

The policy is dated 2021 on its cover and states no end date for itself (only a 2039 middle-income vision), and the text is the document hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site mocti.gov.sl. Text public: yes.

The strategy says the Government of Sierra Leone, under President Julius Maada Bio, 'has developed' the 10-year National Innovation and Digital Strategy 2019-2029, covering digital identity, economy and governance; it names no adopting act or approving body.

The strategy states a 2019-2029 period and is the text itself, hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site mocti.gov.sl, with a running footer 'Last Updated: November 1st, 2019'; it says it will be updated every 3-5 years. Text public: yes.

The strategy lists short-term activities and medium-term target activities dated 2021 to 2025, with no costs, and says it is high-level and that more detailed sector implementation plans will be developed later.

The strategy says a national authority instituted by law 'must be established' to guide the digital transformation, and that a consortium of national institutions will set digital identity standards; no body is yet mandated to deliver it.

The document describes the National Innovation and Digital Strategy (DSTI, 2019) as laying out the plan 'for the next 10 years' to develop infrastructure and human-resource capacity, which puts the period at about 2019-2029; it says nothing on whether the text is published or on the strategy's scope. Text public: not stated.

The ITC report says the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI) 'launched' the National Innovation and Digital Strategy in 2019, 'offering a roadmap for Sierra Leone's future in the tech sector'; no adopting act is named.

The broadband strategy lists the National Digital Development Policy and Strategy among relevant policies that 'have already been developed', and describes the National Digital Development Strategy as a national strategy that is a blueprint for the digital ecosystem; it names no adopting act or body and gives no date for the Strategy, so the document's published date is used.

The document says the National Digital Development Strategy, which stemmed from the National Digital Development Policy, includes two action points on broadband, one being to extend broadband access to all government institutions, including councils, schools, hospitals and libraries, within five years; no cost is given.

The document refers to the 'draft' National Digital Transformation Roadmap (NDTR), which expects a second internet exchange point by 2025; no finalisation or adoption is stated and no date is given for it, so the document's published date is used.

The health roadmap says the Universal Access Development Fund was 'established through' the National Digital Development Policy in the Ministry of Communications, Technology, and Innovations, as a funding source for universal access; the document does not describe the policy's scope.

The World Bank says the National Innovation and Digital Strategy 2019-2029 was 'drafted and launched in 2019' by the Directorate of Science, Technology, and Innovation under the State House, as the high-level vision for the digital economy that prioritises digital government services and digital identification; no adopting act is named.
The World Bank gives the National Innovation and Digital Strategy's period as 2019-2029 and does not say whether its text is published or link to it. Text public: not stated.
